recentItems.title: Saudi Arabia's oil crisis tests the limits of US power | The Dip Podcast
recentItems.description:
Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was meant to keep oil moving when the Strait of Hormuz became dangerous. Attacks on its pumping stations and threats to Red Sea shipping have exposed the limits of that escape route. Energy analyst Kate Dourian and Saudi political-economy researcher Andrew Leber join Daniel Winter to explain the cost of moving oil through a war zone, why disruptions can spread through diesel and transport, and what Riyadh's reported appeal to China reveals about its continuing dependence on US security. #DWbusiness #DWdip

recentItems.title: At least 27 dead in separate mass shootings | DW News
recentItems.description:
One of the shootings happened near Johannesburg, the other outside Cape Town. Police say eight gunmen armed with assault rifles stormed a bar on Saturday evening in Wedela township, west of Johannesburg. Hours later, gunmen opened fire at an entertainment venue in a township outside Cape Town. Ten people were killed and eleven wounded.

recentItems.title: Hundreds of thousands attend Pope Leo's open-air Mass | DW News
recentItems.description:
Hundreds of thousands of people packed Paris' iconic Champs-Élysées avenue to attend an open-air Mass with Pope Leo XIV on Saturday, a sign of the Catholic Church's enduring appeal in the once staunchly Catholic but officially secular country. The Vatican estimated that 800,000 people attended — about 200,000 more than the number who had registered in advance.

recentItems.title: 100,000 without power as Nor’easter sweeps US East Coast | DW News
recentItems.description:
A massive, unseasonably early Nor'easter is slamming the coastal northeast of the US. From New York to Boston, tens of millions of people are bracing for high winds, heavy rains, and dangerous coastal waves throughout the weekend. The intense fall storm has already knocked out power to around 100,000 residents and conditions are only getting worse. Joining us from Maine to explain the science is Matthew Cappucci, Senior Meteorologist at MyRadar.

recentItems.title: Germany and Russia hold first high-level talks since full-scale Ukraine invasion | DW News
recentItems.description:
Germany and Russia's foreign ministers have met for the first time since before Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Johann Wadephul and Sergei Lavrov held brief talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. The meeting comes amid sharply worsening relations between Berlin and Moscow, just weeks after Germany accused Russia of being behind an attempted drone attack on Leipzig/Halle airport.
Wadephul called on Russia to abandon what Germany described as its "dangerous path of escalation" towards Germany, Europe and NATO. So why did Berlin open a direct diplomatic channel with Moscow now, and could Germany's role in the Ukraine war be changing?
DW's Benjamin Alvarez Gruber reports from the United Nations.

recentItems.title: Bangkok flooded: Nearly 300mm of rain leaves Thai capital struggling | DW News
recentItems.description:
Bangkok has been declared a disaster area after days of torrential rain flooded homes, businesses and major roads across the Thai capital.
Nearly 300 millimetres of rain fell in some areas in less than 48 hours, overwhelming Bangkok's canals and drainage system. Residents have been forced to wade through deep floodwaters, while schools, businesses and transport have been disrupted.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt says the situation has stabilised, but more heavy rain is forecast and authorities are still trying to manage water flowing into the city from neighbouring provinces.
Journalist Tommy Walker reports from Bangkok on how residents are coping, whether the city is prepared for further rainfall, and how the flooding compares with Thailand's devastating 2011 floods.
